surface_forms: celle qui était le plus près de lui

appraisal_events.evidence: Mais déjà Elstir avait quitté les jeunes filles sans m'avoir appelé. Elles prirent une rue de traverse, il vint vers moi. Tout était manqué.
appraisal_events.explanation: Having elaborately staged an air of indifference while waiting to be called over and introduced, the narrator misses his chance entirely when Elstir says goodbye to the girls without presenting him; the narrating voice bluntly seals this as a total local failure ('Tout était manqué').

status_effects.explanation: The narrator is shut out of the anticipated introduction to the petite bande (including Albertine), the very encounter he had contrived to appear unconcerned about, and the passage frames this outcome unambiguously as failure.

ambiguities: It is unclear whether the failed introduction is best read as an oversight by Elstir or as a consequence of the narrator's own contrived aloofness (he deliberately hung back and looked away); the passage attributes it to circumstance rather than a deliberate slight, so the diminishment is coded as self/narratorial (source: narrator) rather than as an act by Elstir.

The passage's extended reflection on how belief inflates or deflates the perceived value of Albertine (rendered 'presque insignifiante puis infiniment précieuse' within seconds) is a genuine double movement, but since it cancels itself out as psychological volatility rather than a stable local outcome, it was not coded as a separate appraisal event.
